chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Whether McRae led bands of his own
summary: He says the McRae Brothers was his only early band and that he led big bands in 1945-47.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah. All right. Well, before we start talking about the Chick Webb period, is there anything up to that period -- up to, say, the early part of 1936 -- that anything else you want to talk about that we may have missed or...?
Let me -- there's one question here. It says, I think, it was in Chilton's Who's Who. That you had your own band, or was that merely the McRae Brothers Band that you --
No, that was later.
This was back in 1927, was
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
No, that was the McRae Brothers Band.
But that wasn't -- You never had a band of your own as such.
I had a band after --
Oh, you did.
That was in '47.
But you didn't --
After I had left -- I think it was Cab, or somebody like that. '45 or '47, I had a couple of bands, big bands that I had put together.
I see. But you didn't have any, say, during the Depression or just before the Depression -- leader of bands?
No, I didn't have no bands after that. I mean, that I know of. Might've been just like a little gig band, or something like that.
Most all the musicians had, you know --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Have gig bands.
-- have gig bands. You know, (Inaudible) gigs -- club dates and things like that. I might've had something like that.
Because everybody was gigging from the time, you know -- making it -- trying to make it, you know. The Gigs were was the top thing.
That's where the musicians made their living, just gigging, you know.
